newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil sees cost savings on Aasgard with new valve.
newsitem.headline: Statoil sees cost savings on Aasgard with new valve.

text.p: Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) said on Thursday a new type of fast-acting valve to be adopted on the Aasgard development could lead to savings of up to one billion crowns.

The high integrity pressure protection system (Hipps) will be installed for gas production on the Aasgard B floater and will eliminate the need for a separate flare stack, Statoil's Status Weekly newsletter said.
Installed at the inlet to each riser -- a tube that carries oil and gas from the seabed to the production unit -- the valve closes when pressure exceeds design capacity of the processing facilities.
Statoil said Hipps technology was a more environmental-friendly solution than the traditional approach of venting gas through the flare system.
The valves have already been used in the Zeepipe and Europipe I trunklines to continental Europe, the Kaarstoe and Kollsnes gas treatment plants and the Sleipner B platform.
